answer_correct.note: both annotators decided on 177 rows; 7 disagreements, all a1=yes a2=no, adjudicated yes (paraphrase/equivalence cases)

evidence_sufficient.note: kappa degenerate: a2 never said no (183 yes / 17 uncertain), a1 said no 37 times with substantive notes; all 20 disagreements were a1=no a2=yes, adjudicated no (notes cite missing facts or unresolvable temporal anchors per README rule 3)

key_findings.stored_failure_labels: of 60 stored-incorrect rows with a human verdict, humans confirm 54 (90.0%); the failure-label base rate is mostly sound
key_findings.judge_abstention_false_positives: of 66 sampled stored-correct rows, 20 (30.3%) are human-adjudicated wrong; 13 of the 20 are abstention-style answers ('Not mentioned', 'Cannot be determined') the judge accepted as correct — abstention FPs inflate semantic accuracy and would contaminate any F6/accuracy comparison
key_findings.gate_sensitivity: the stored evidence gate misses real insufficiency: of 85 stored-insufficient rows humans confirm only ~20 sufficient-side errors and vice versa; gate recall 0.564 (misses 65 truly-insufficient rows) — E0 counts are unreliable in both directions
key_findings.kappa_gate_near_zero: gate kappa ~0.03-0.07 vs human adjudication: the automatic gate is statistically near-independent of human sufficiency judgements; any E0-based claim needs the human-corrected gate
